Verified that the sink m_os->open() uses std::ofstream::open, which opens a file directly via the C++ standard library and does not invoke a shell or any command interpreter. No path from m_name to system(), exec, or popen is present. Even if m_name contains characters such as spaces, semicolons, or newlines, they are treated as literal parts of the file path, not as command separators. Therefore, OS Command Injection is not possible.

No additional checks or neutralizations are needed because the operation is inherently safe against command injection.
